title: Sensex Rallies 427 Points to 82,532 as Bank Stocks Power Second Straight Gain
excerpt: The Nifty closed at 25,387, its highest in nine months, as the Nifty Bank index hit a record 62,442 and foreign investors kept buying despite a weak global trend.
body:
• The BSE Sensex rallied 427.40 points, or 0.52%, to settle at 82,532.19 on Tuesday, November 17, and the NSE Nifty climbed 96.30 points, or 0.38%, to 25,387.40 — a second straight day of gains.
  • Banking stocks led the rally: the Nifty Bank index surged 866.3 points, or 1.4%, to a fresh record high of 62,442.20.
  • Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth Rs 4,864.68 crore on Monday, according to exchange data, while domestic institutional investors sold Rs 3,519.05 crore on a net basis.
  • For NRI investors, the rupee ended at 93.47 per dollar on Tuesday, against a previous close of 93.93, as Indian benchmarks rose despite a weak global trend.

Indian benchmark indices extended their rally for a second straight day on Tuesday, with the Sensex climbing 427.40 points and the Nifty ending at 25,387.40, driven by steady foreign fund inflows, moderate crude oil prices and buying in Reliance Industries and bank stocks, PTI reported.

The 30-share BSE Sensex rallied 427.40 points, or 0.52 per cent, to settle at 82,532.19. During the day it surged 792.7 points, or 0.96 per cent, to an intraday high of 82,897.49. The 50-share NSE Nifty climbed 96.30 points, or 0.38 per cent, to end at 25,387.40, after touching a session peak of 25,501.35. The close took the Nifty to its highest level in nine months, recovering the losses recorded since February 27, according to market reports.

Banks set the pace

The Nifty Bank index surged 866.3 points, or 1.4%, to a fresh record high of 62,442.20, surpassing its previous all-time high of 61,764.85, Upstox reported from exchange data. Among Sensex stocks, Axis Bank, Reliance Industries, State Bank of India, Tata Consultancy Services, Adani Ports and Mahindra & Mahindra were among the major winners, PTI reported. On the Nifty, Adani Enterprises led the gainers, closing 3.24% higher a day after its subsidiary Adani Wind began production of the country's longest wind turbine blade, 91.2 metres, at its plant in Mundra, Gujarat. Eicher Motors rose 3.01%, Max Healthcare 2.08%, Asian Paints 2.02% and Axis Bank 1.98%.

IT and utility stocks lagged. HCL Technologies fell 2.09%, Power Grid 1.60%, HDFC Life 1.56%, ONGC 1.53% and Coal India 1.50% among the top Nifty losers; PTI also listed Tech Mahindra and Infosys among the Sensex laggards. The broader market was mixed: the Nifty Midcap 100 closed at 61,730, up 153.60 points or 0.25%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 ended at 19,398.70, down 42.40 points or 0.22%.

Flows, crude and the global backdrop

Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth Rs 4,864.68 crore on Monday, according to exchange data cited by PTI; domestic institutional investors sold equities worth Rs 3,519.05 crore on a net basis, Upstox reported. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was up 0.26 per cent at USD 92.68 per barrel, PTI reported.

The gains came against a weak global trend. In Asia, South Korea's Kospi, Japan's Nikkei 225, Shanghai's SSE Composite and Hong Kong's Hang Seng all ended lower, and European markets were trading in negative territory. US markets had ended lower on Monday, with the Nasdaq Composite down 2.49 per cent, the S&P 500 down 1.92 per cent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 1.41 per cent.

On Monday, the Sensex had climbed 512.34 points, or 0.63 per cent, to settle at 82,104.79, and the Nifty rose 146.80 points, or 0.58 per cent, to 25,291.10. What to watch next is whether foreign inflows sustain a third session and whether the Nifty can hold above the 25,500 level it briefly crossed on Tuesday.
